target.artifact: deterministic portfolio allocation auditor plus durable selection receipt
target.consumer: fresh /wc workers, Live projection, swarm verifier

title: Make portfolio fallback allocation auditable
problem: Portfolio fallback is now a binding allocation layer, but there is no required machine-auditable receipt that explains why each higher-priority seed/derived job was skipped and why a worker legitimately crossed into generic discovery. This fresh /wc observed a fully saturated seed frontier: Live had a terminal DONE return, every other seed job had a claim directory, and the derived root was absent. Establishing that state required manual multi-read reconciliation, so the fallback canary is not independently reconstructable from one deterministic allocator result.
mission: Build a read-only deterministic portfolio allocation auditor that consumes PORTFOLIO.json, derived jobs, claim expiries and terminal returns; emits ordered per-job dispositions with exact evidence; and produces a snapshot receipt proving either the next claimable job or DISCOVERY_ALLOWED. Keep create-if-absent claims as the authority boundary and never let an allocation receipt self-promote product state.
acceptance: Seed and valid derived jobs are merged by the same priority/value rules as WORKER_CONTRACT_V1.
Every candidate receives one explicit disposition: CLAIMABLE, ACTIVE_CLAIM, TERMINAL_RETURN, DUPLICATE_DERIVED, AUTHORITY_BLOCKED or INVALID, with exact evidence refs.
Claim expiry is evaluated from claim content; directory existence alone never blocks work forever.
Missing coordination/portfolio/derived is represented explicitly as an empty source with SOURCE_DEBT/evidence, not interpreted as proof of no future successors.
The result carries source head, observed epoch and deterministic ordering so independent workers can reproduce the same snapshot decision.
The auditor never replaces atomic create-if-absent claim acquisition; a race loser must reload and re-evaluate.
A fixture matching the observed canary state — Live terminal DONE, nine active seed claims, no derived root — returns DISCOVERY_ALLOWED and no claimable seed job.
A second fixture with one expired claim exposes that job as CLAIMABLE while preserving the expired claim as evidence.

observed_live_evidence.note: Active-vs-expired semantics must be evaluated from claim contents in the implementation; this discovery proposal does not infer perpetual blocking from directory existence.

value_signals.unblock_value: Lets fresh workers prove why no portfolio job is currently safe to claim and cross into discovery without human inspection or accidental duplicate work.
value_signals.compounding_value: As derived jobs begin reproducing, one allocator view can merge seed and generated work while preserving deterministic dedupe/expiry semantics.
value_signals.human_friction_reduction: Removes the need for a guide or human to inspect many claim/return directories when identical /wc workers saturate the frontier.
value_signals.information_gain: Turns portfolio fallback from a prose contract into a falsifiable, snapshot-reconstructable decision boundary.

risk.main: A stale receipt could be mistaken for current authority while other workers mutate claims/returns concurrently.
risk.mitigation: Receipts are snapshot evidence only, always carry source head/epoch, and never authorize a claim; workers must reload and atomically create the actual job claim.

falsification: Two independent evaluations of the same repository snapshot disagree on ordered job dispositions.
A terminally returned job is emitted CLAIMABLE.
A non-expired active claim is ignored or an expired claim blocks forever.
Missing derived root crashes allocation or is silently treated as proof that no successor work exists.
The receipt itself is accepted as mutation authority without a create-if-absent claim race.
Observed saturated fixture fails to produce DISCOVERY_ALLOWED.
dedup_note: Repository search found no existing portfolio allocator skip-reason/selection receipt proposal. This is narrower than the role-fluid allocator and does not duplicate Live portfolio projection or G2->G3 autonomy work; it specifically makes the new portfolio fallback boundary machine-auditable.

source_freshness.note: Main was moving concurrently; this proposal is append-only candidate evidence and does not claim the observed snapshot remains current after publication.
